faqs.question: What should I text my crush on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Pick one brief message about something you have in common and close on an easy question, like a candy debate or a costume reveal. Match it to how well you know them: a new number gets a light poll, a friend you like gets a callback joke, and someone you already text can get a plan.

faqs.question: What time should I text my crush on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Between 2 pm and 8 pm on Halloween suits most people, because they are getting ready and still looking at their phone. After 11 pm, only reply to messages they send; do not start a new thread.

faqs.question: How long should I wait for my crush to reply?
faqs.answer: Give it until the next morning for a first text, and longer on a party night. In one study of real teen texts, even replies to an established partner averaged about 9 minutes, and replies to friends about 14 minutes, so a crush taking hours on Halloween is normal.

faqs.question: Should I double text my crush if they don't answer?
faqs.answer: One gentle follow-up after a real wait is fine, for example a no-pressure note the next day. If that also goes unanswered, stop; a third message adds pressure and rarely changes the outcome.

faqs.question: Is it weird to text a classmate or coworker on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Not if the text stays about the place you share, such as a deadline, a shift or a teacher's costume. Keep comments on their appearance out of it, so things stay comfortable on Monday whatever they reply.

faqs.question: Which emoji are okay in a Halloween text to a crush?
faqs.answer: One themed emoji, such as a ghost or a pumpkin, placed at the end of the message is enough. Hearts and kissing faces read as a confession from someone they have just met, so save them for later.

faqs.question: Can I send my crush a Halloween meme or GIF?
faqs.answer: Yes, once they have sent you one first and it is about something you both know, like a film or a class. As an opening message a GIF gives them nothing to answer, so start with words.

faqs.question: How do I turn a Halloween text into a plan to hang out?
faqs.answer: Name one activity, one day and an easy exit in the same message, for example a scary film this weekend followed by 'totally fine if not'. A clear yes means agreeing a time and place straight away; a vague answer is a no for now.

faqs.question: Should I send my crush a Halloween page instead of a text?
faqs.answer: Not as a first move. The standard SubhSandesh Halloween card ends on a boo question where the No button runs away, which suits a partner but not someone deciding whether to say yes, so keep any page for after they have agreed to a date.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is always 31 October: a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027. All Saints' Day follows on 1 November, which makes the next morning a natural moment for a follow-up text.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Texts to Send Your Crush, Sorted by How Well You Know Them

The best Halloween texts to send your crush are short, tied to something you both know, and finish on a question that takes five seconds to answer. Send it between 2 pm and 8 pm on Halloween (Saturday 31 October 2026; Sunday 31 October 2027), then let them set the pace.

Of all views of SubhSandesh pages, 48.3% come from phones, and 38.5% of the people making one lock it with a password, so assume your words get read privately on a phone. Below: 24 original openers by closeness, a send-time table, follow-ups, emoji rules and six texts to avoid.

## What should a Halloween message for a crush do?

A Halloween message for a crush is a light, low-stakes text that borrows the date as its reason to start a conversation, not a declaration of feelings.

In the Pew Research Center's 2014–15 survey of American teens (ages 13 to 17), 31% had sent flirtatious messages to someone they liked, rising to 63% of teens with dating experience against 14% of those without ([Pew Research Center, 2015](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2015/10/01/teens-technology-and-romantic-relationships/)). Playful texts land best after some real-life contact, so every opener below assumes you have met.

## 24 Halloween texts to send your crush, by how well you know them

Each group gives the job, six openers and the next move. Add one real detail (their costume, the class): specific reads as attention, generic as a forward.

### 1. You just got their number

Job: say who you are and hand them an easy reply. Twenty words is plenty.

- "Hi, it's [name] from [place]. Settling a debate: are you a candy corn defender or a hater?"
- "[Name] here 👻 Saving myself in your phone as 'the ghost from Thursday' unless you've got a better idea."
- "Quick poll before the sugar rush: full-size chocolate bars or minis? Asking for scientific reasons."
- "Hey, it's [name]. Best costume you've ever pulled off? Mine involved a bedsheet and regret."
- "Costume reveal now, or are you keeping it classified until tonight?"
- "Hi! I just passed a house with 14 inflatable pumpkins. What's the most over-the-top display near you?"

Next move: a question back means they're playing along. Answer, ask one thing, then stop for the day.

### 2. A classmate or coworker you see every week

Job: stay friendly enough that Monday isn't awkward. Mention the shared place, never their looks.

- "Pretty sure the scariest thing this week was that group project deadline. Happy Halloween!"
- "Did you survive [class/shift] or did it survive you? 🎃"
- "If [teacher/manager] turns up in costume on Monday I need a witness. Are you in?"
- "Happy Halloween! What's on tonight: something scary or something with a laugh track?"
- "Still owe you for covering me on Tuesday. I assume payment is accepted in fun-size chocolate only?"
- "Ranking the costumes I saw today and yours made the podium. The winner stays anonymous."

Next move: keep the thread on your shared world for now; suggest meeting outside class or work only once the chat runs on its own.

### 3. A friend you've started to like

Job: sound like you, since they know your texting voice. Turn the warmth up one notch, no more.

- "Spooky season update: the seat next to me for horror films is still reserved for you."
- "Remember when you screamed at the cat in [film]? Rewatching it tonight in your honour."
- "Every Halloween has been more fun with you around. Okay, cheesy. Want to do something scary this weekend?"
- "Wearing the costume you talked me into. If I look ridiculous, that's on you."
- "Honest question: if the two of us went as a duo, which pair would we be?"
- "Honestly, yours are the only Halloween photos I'm waiting for tonight."

Next move: if they match the warmth, invite them to one specific thing. If they reply like a friend, accept that and keep it easy.

### 4. Someone you've already been texting

Job: turn chatting into a plan without a speech. Name a day, an activity and an exit.

- "I have a Halloween proposal: one scary film, two snacks of your choice, this weekend. Thoughts?"
- "Decided you're my official Halloween text. Everyone else gets the group message."
- "You've been on my mind all week, and not in a haunted way. Free on the 31st?"
- "What's the costume tonight? I'd like a photo, strictly for judging purposes."
- "If you're not busy once trick-or-treat hours wind down, I know a good hot chocolate place. Totally fine if not."
- "Trick or treat: I tell you something embarrassing about me, or you tell me your plans for Friday."

Next move: a clear yes means fixing a time and place right there. Anything vaguer is a no for now.

## When to send it on 31 October: a timing table

Both years put Halloween on a weekend, so most people are free by day and out by evening. Aim for the window before their plans start, while they're getting ready and still checking their phone.

| Send window | Best for | What to send | If no reply, wait until |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2–5 pm | Just got their number; classmate or coworker | A poll or one easy question | The next morning |
| 5–8 pm | A friend you like | A costume photo or a callback joke | After 10 pm, then stop |
| 8–11 pm | Someone you've been texting | A short plan for the weekend | Midday on 1 November |
| After 11 pm | Nobody, unless they texted first | Nothing new; replies only | Not applicable |
| Morning of 1 November | Anyone who replied | A "how was your night?" follow-up | 2 November, then let it go |

The waits in the last column are generous on purpose. In a study that logged the real texts of 214 US high-school students (from August 2008), the average reply to a romantic partner took 9.27 minutes, to friends 14.5 minutes and to parents 50.39 minutes ([Ehrenreich et al., 2020](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8669751)). On a party night, a crush can take hours and still be interested.

## Follow-ups if they reply, and if they don't

If they reply, match their length and energy and add one question; a two-line answer gets two lines back.

- "Ha, I knew you'd say that. Next question: which horror film have you never managed to watch to the end?"
- "That costume deserves an award. Did you make it or buy it?"
- "Glad your night was good. Mine got better around 7 pm, for no particular reason. 🎃"
- "Want to compare candy hauls tomorrow? I'll bring the evidence."

No reply? Send one gentle follow-up after the wait in the table, then go quiet.

- "No pressure to answer, hope the night was fun!"
- "Happy 1 November. Still curious about the candy corn verdict whenever you surface."
- "All good if you're busy. See you on Monday."

Silence after one follow-up is an answer. A 2024 study of 26 Tinder users in Ljubljana described ghosting as an undesirable but normalised way to disconnect, used for self-protection or to cope with message overload ([Šiša, 2024](https://www.cogitatiopress.com/mediaandcommunication/article/view/8563)). That says little about you, and it's reason enough to skip a third message.

## Emoji, memes and GIFs: what's the right dose?

Use one emoji per text, and a Halloween one only on the day. The Unicode Consortium's 2019 frequency ranking puts 😂 and ❤️ at the top, while 👻 sits in group 7 (under 1/128 as common as 😂) and 🎃 in group 10 (under 1/1,024) ([Unicode Consortium, 2019](https://home.unicode.org/emoji/emoji-frequency/)). Rare symbols stand out: one ghost reads as on-theme, three read as trying hard.

- A single emoji, placed last, never as the whole reply.
- Skip ❤️, 😍 and 😘 early on; out of context they read as a declaration.
- Memes and GIFs only after they've sent one, and only about your shared thing.

## 6 Halloween texts never to send a crush

In the same Pew survey, 35% of teen girls had blocked or unfriended someone because of flirting that made them uncomfortable, against 16% of boys. Most of what gets a person muted is below.

- Anything sexual, including "sexy costume" remarks or innuendo about treats; from a near-stranger it never lands as a joke.
- Comments on their body in a costume photo. Compliment the idea or the effort instead.
- Double texts after 11 pm, especially "u up?" or "why didn't you answer?"
- A screenshot of their reply forwarded to your group chat, or posted anywhere.
- A guilt line such as "I made this for you, the least you can do is reply."
- A pickup line copied from a 300-line listicle; it tells them nothing about you.

## After a yes: when a Halloween page beats another text

A text opens the door; a page marks the moment after. Both SubhSandesh Halloween pages end by asking them to be your boo, and on the standard version the No button keeps fleeing, so only yes sticks. Fine for a partner, wrong for a first ask where no must be as easy as yes: use them only after your crush has agreed to a date, or once you're together.

- The [haunted-house Halloween card with a pumpkin to carve](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) suits a quick, playful thank-you: up to six photos, your letter revealed by torchlight in an attic, roughly five minutes to put together.
- The [premium Halloween page that plays your voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) fits a bigger moment: a voice note capped at 60 seconds, up to a dozen photos, an optional unlock time, and a single 280-character reply that lands in your email; roughly ten minutes to build.
- If they said yes to a plan rather than to being your boo, an [invitation page they answer, which then counts the days down](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) keeps it light.

SubhSandesh pages average 11.1 views apiece, so they get revisited far more than one text does. The limits: one recipient per page, English-language screens, and no help meeting anyone new. If the chat is three messages old, a link is too much; send a text.

## Sources

- Pew Research Center (Lenhart, Anderson & Smith), [Teens, Technology and Romantic Relationships](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2015/10/01/teens-technology-and-romantic-relationships/), 1 October 2015.
- Ehrenreich, Beron, Burnell, Meter & Underwood, [How Adolescents Use Text Messaging Through their High School Years](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8669751), Journal of Research on Adolescence 30(2), 2020.
- Šiša, [Ghosting on Tinder: Examining Disconnectivity in Online Dating](https://www.cogitatiopress.com/mediaandcommunication/article/view/8563), Media and Communication 12, 24 October 2024.
- Unicode Consortium, [The Most Frequent Emoji, 2019](https://home.unicode.org/emoji/emoji-frequency/).
